proof.text: For any partial closed structure, inverse transposition of a is tensor(a, identity) followed by evaluation. Naturality of the realization tensorator and the ambient adjunction identify the realized transpose with postcomposition by the specified comparison. This is a calculation in the given structures; no finite-stage existence theorem is required.

The ordinary realization is the composite of R.J with the derived section functor. R.fully_faithful makes the first functor fully faithful, and the presentation equivalence makes the second fully faithful. Compose the source inverse-transpose equivalence, the realization map equivalence, precomposition with the tensorator, and ambient transposition. The previous calculation identifies this composite with the realization map followed by postcomposition with c. Since the realization map is bijective, postcomposition by c is bijective on every realized test object.

Apply the existing core boundedness theorem to Q. Its witness and R.image give a common-stage object L and an isomorphism t from its ordinary realization to Q. Surjectivity of the previous Hom bijection gives s with s followed by c equal to t.hom. Define b = t.inv followed by s. Then b followed by c is the identity. Injectivity of the same Hom bijection with test object H shows c followed by b is the identity. Thus the actual evaluation transpose c is invertible.

Uncurry the two sides of pair naturality. The ambient source-variable evaluation law and counit naturality compute the right side. Tensorator naturality and normalizedCommonEvaluationForStructure_naturality identify it with the left side; injectivity of inverse transposition proves the equation. Finally the inverse-transpose formula applied to transpose(realizedEvaluation) is exactly the required evaluation equation.
